regularizer.why: No beta gave a styled gain significantly above 0, so the sweep is too short to tell: beta 0.1, a light brake that lets learning happen; exploitation stays guarded by the safety net and measured by the explorer test.

safetyNet.method: The exported adaptive model (int8) with the Zap knobs under each safety net setting, against the 11 training styles (G) and the 6 proxy explorers (P), paired pair by pair with the same model with the statistics at no evidence (seed a5). Stage 1: every setting, 250 duplicate pairs per segment per opponent per setting. Stage 2: the shortlist (finite settings with a stage 1 mean P of at most 0.5 point, the 3 with the best G) on new deals, 1500 pairs per segment per opponent. Pooled intervals count each deal once across opponents (the opponents share the deals). The net bounds the distribution each character plays (knobs and temperature applied before it); lambdaBelow1Share, topChangedShare, meanKlPlayed and meanTvPlayed are per decision of the adaptive seats.
safetyNet.why: Among the stage 2 settings whose proxy explorer gain has a 95% upper bound of at most 0.5 point, the one with the best styled gain (b0.5-h1; ties go to the tighter setting).

explorer.method: Re-measure, no new search: the explorer chosen by the search of attempt 3 (training/runs/m6-adaptive/eval/explorer-search-3.json, made against another adaptive file with the safety net {"bmax":0.2,"nHalf":1}) played again against this file (safety net {"bmax":0.2,"nHalf":1}) on fresh deals. Explorer: style a, then style b, on v1, switching at a hand or once its seat has shown a number of betting events (partner in 2 against 2: the same schedule or v1 Zap). Search on selection deals (seed e5, pairs from 2720 per segment, after the earlier searches) over 1008 of 1008 candidates by successive halving against the adaptive network and the ablated network, ranked by the adaptation part. The chosen explorer then played 2000 fresh duplicate pairs per segment (seed f7, pairs 14000 to 15999, never played by an earlier attempt) against the adaptive network, the twin and the ablated network, with the Zap knobs. Gain: score of the explorer against the adaptive network minus its score against the twin, pair by pair; adaptation part: score against the adaptive network minus score against the ablated network. playedOutsideTraining: of the explorer's fresh matches against each player, the share whose realized play no training draw of the adaptive network's family plays exactly, seat by seat and hand by hand given the betting events each seat had shown (styles.ts explorerMatchInFamily: a feint in its hand or evidence range, a switching player in its hand range, a stable extreme, or a feint whose switch never came; three phases or a held-out style that played are outside); share is the one against the adaptive network. An explorer outside the training family by its label is scored mostly on play a training draw also plays when that share is small. Pass under the rule of attempt 1 (superseded on 2026-11-22 by explorer.criterion; pass and passTwinRule): every explorer measured has a one-sided 95% upper bound of the gain over the twin of at most 1 point. passAdaptationPart: the same bound on the adaptation part, the rule of explorer.criterion.

trained.method: A network trained with PPO as a best response against the adaptive network as served when it trained (training/runs/m6-adaptive-r/export/zap-v2-b0.2-h1.zapw: statistics live, safety net {"bmax":0.2,"nHalf":1}, Zap knobs), holding the other team; the explorer holds both seats of its team in 2 against 2. Start: training/runs/m6-explorer-init/start.zapw, folded from the twin file training/runs/m6-twin/export/zap-v2.zapw, not the twin measured below (training/runs/m6-twin-r/export/zap-v2.zapw) (training/explorer_init.py moves its weights on the statistics into the bias, so it starts by playing as that file, exactly except for a small interaction term in mineiro 2 against 2: training.startFold and training.startCheck). Features v2-self: its own public statistics, the next seat's and its partner's, so it sees what the adaptive network reads about it and how many hands have gone by. One episode per match, so early play is credited with later hands. 98 PPO iterations after 5 of critic warm-up, 12366974 decisions, 3 workers and 3 learner threads, 76.4 minutes. Periodic check every 10 iterations: 200 pairs per segment (seed 3e) against the adaptive network and the ablated one. Measured on fresh deals (seed f8, pairs 0 to 1999 per segment, a seed no other bench uses), duplicate format, the explorer with neutral knobs against the adaptive network (training/runs/m6-adaptive-r/export/zap-v2-b0.2-h1.zapw, safety net {"bmax":0.2,"nHalf":1}), the ablated network (same file, statistics at no evidence), the twin and the second twin, all with the Zap knobs. Adaptation part: score against the adaptive network minus score against the ablated one, pair by pair (primary criterion: one-sided 95% upper bound at most 1 point). Gain over the twin: score against the adaptive network minus score against the twin; seed floor seen by this explorer: score against the second twin minus score against the twin. Style: 500 matches per segment (seed f9) of the explorer and of its start against the adaptive network, public statistics of the explorer's seats by hand of the match. The twin has 590 training iterations and the second twin 390, so score against the second twin minus score against the twin mixes the seeds with that extra training: it is not a seed floor here.

style.words: Not described by a person yet; the style numbers only, against the adaptive network, for hands 1 to 3, 4 to 6 and 7 on: asked for truco in 35.8, 33.4, 31.8% (its start: 36.6, 35.2, 33.3%) of its hands; ran from 63.8, 64.8, 68.7% (its start: 45.5, 50.1, 56.3%) of the bets it answered; raised again in 6.4, 9.0, 8.6% (its start: 10.4, 9.7, 8.6%) of them; covered 14.7, 16.0, 18.9% (its start: 21.0, 21.9, 22.3%) of the plays where covering was allowed.

criterion.method: Primary criterion of the explorer test: for every explorer measured on fresh deals against the file that would be served, the one-sided 95% upper bound of the adaptation part (score against the adaptive network minus score against the ablated network, the same file with the statistics at no evidence, pair by pair) is at most 1 point. The gain over the twin is reported next to it with the seed floor, for context. Verdicts recomputed from the stored fresh results of every attempt, of the trained explorer and of the control explorer when it was measured. Only the results whose adaptive file (models.adaptive.sha256) is the served file (servedModel) count, in verdicts; the results measured against earlier files are listed in history with their result file, model file and safety net, and do not count. pass is false while no explorer was measured against the served file, and while an explorer that failed against an earlier file has no verdict against the served file (pendingRemeasure lists them: a new search that passes does not replace measuring a known exploiter again). What was searched: the scripted search of attempt 1 ranked its candidates by the gain over the twin (safety net Bmax 0.5, nHalf 1); attempt 2 ranked its candidates by the adaptation part (safety net Bmax 0.5, nHalf 1); attempt 3 ranked its candidates by the adaptation part (safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1); attempt 4 measured the explorer of attempt 2 again, with no new search (safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1); attempt 5 ranked its candidates by the adaptation part (safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1); attempt 6 measured the explorer of attempt 1 again, with no new search (safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1); attempt 7 measured the explorer of attempt 2 again, with no new search (safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1); attempt 8 measured the explorer of attempt 3 again, with no new search (safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1). The trained explorer stopped after 103 iterations (98 of them PPO), 76.4 minutes (max-hours 3), of the 103 planned; it trained against training/runs/m6-adaptive-r/export/zap-v2-b0.2-h1.zapw (SHA-256 7223c227, safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1). An explorer trained for an earlier file and measured against the served file counts too (verdicts.otherTrained). The control explorer (trained against the twin, explorer.control) is an explorer measured too, so its verdict counts.
criterion.why: This criterion was set on 2026-11-22 after attempt 1 failed the rule written before it (gain over the twin, one-sided 95% upper bound at most 1 point), and before the trained explorer was measured. It judges the file that would be served (SHA-256 7223c227, safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1): only the 9 verdicts measured against that file count; the 9 measured against earlier files are listed in explorer.criterion.history with their file and net, and do not count. Against the file with safety net Bmax 0.5, nHalf 1 (SHA-256 45c541c5), the explorer of attempt 2, trapper>bluffer@3/v1, has an adaptation part of 0.83 (from 0.50 to 1.15) points, one-sided 95% upper bound 1.10: above 1 point, so that file fails the criterion. Against the file with safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1 (SHA-256 fa30e9a5), the explorer of attempt 4, trapper>bluffer@3/v1, has an adaptation part of 0.79 (from 0.49 to 1.10) points, one-sided 95% upper bound 1.05: above 1 point, so that file fails the criterion. Every explorer that failed against an earlier file was measured again against this one, on fresh deals: trapper>bluffer@3/v1 0.26 (from -0.04 to 0.55) points, upper bound 0.50. Under the old rule 3 of the 8 explorers aimed at the adaptive network and measured against this file fail (upper bounds of the gain over the twin -0.29, -0.43, 1.10, -0.41, 0.31, -0.50, 4.44, 1.89 points, in the order of explorer.criterion.verdicts: scripted attempts, then the trained explorer, then the explorers trained for earlier files; the control explorer trained against the twin and is left out). For the scripted explorers of attempt 1 (safety net Bmax 0.5, nHalf 1) and attempt 6 (safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1), searched for the gain over the twin, that gain (0.78, 1.15, 0.62, -0.87 points) is about the size of the seed floor. For the trained explorer it is not: its seed floor is 0.99 (from 0.17 to 1.81), and its 4.76 point base part is play learned against the adaptive network's weights. The explorer trained for an earlier file (training/runs/m6-adaptive/export/zap-v2-b0.5-h1.zapw, SHA-256 45c541c5, safety net Bmax 0.5, nHalf 1), training/runs/m6-explorer/explorer.zapw, was measured against this one too (training/runs/m6-adaptive-r/eval/history/old-m6-explorer-b0.2-h1.json): adaptation part -0.64 (from -1.18 to -0.11) points, upper bound -0.20. An explorer trained the same way against the twin (explorer.control: same start, seeds and options, 98 PPO iterations, as the trained explorer) scored 56.4% against the twin on new deals (seed fa); on the same deals the trained explorer scored 59.9% against the adaptive network as served and 60.5% against the ablated one. It trained against the twin file training/runs/m6-twin/export/zap-v2.zapw (SHA-256 afdc6096), not the twin measured here (training/runs/m6-twin-r/export/zap-v2.zapw, SHA-256 5bdd9096). The trained explorer's score against the adaptive network as served minus the control's against the twin is 3.44 (from 2.60 to 4.29) points (against the ablated network: 4.08, from 3.23 to 4.92), so a best response of the same budget takes more from the adaptive file as served than from the twin: by this measure the adaptive base is more exploitable, and switching adaptation on would serve it. This comparison is less clean: the trained explorer was measured against the file it trained on, the control against a twin it never trained on. The ablated network is the same file with the statistics at no evidence, so the adaptation part (score against the adaptive network minus score against the ablated one, on the same deals) holds only what the reading changes. It is also the only part the safety net acts on: without evidence the net lets nothing move, so the ablated network, and with it the base part, is the same whatever the net.

control.method: Control of the trained explorer: a network trained exactly as explorer.trained (start training/runs/m6-explorer-init, features v2-self, one episode per match, seeds 7e, the same options) but with the twin as served in the league (Zap knobs; the twin reads nothing) instead of the adaptive network, for the same number of PPO iterations: 98 after 5 of critic warm-up, 12366503 decisions, 3 workers and 3 learner threads, 66.8 minutes. Periodic check every 10 iterations: 200 pairs per segment (seed 3e) against the twin. Measured on new deals (seed fa, pairs 0 to 1999 per segment, a seed no other bench uses), duplicate format, the control and the trained explorer (explorer.trained) each with neutral knobs against the adaptive network as served, the ablated network, the twin and the second twin, all with the Zap knobs. asServed: the trained explorer's score against the adaptive network minus the control's score against the twin, pair by pair on the same deals (how much more a best response of this budget takes from the adaptive file as served than from the twin as served). base: the trained explorer's score against the ablated network minus the control's score against the twin. It trained against the twin file training/runs/m6-twin/export/zap-v2.zapw (SHA-256 afdc6096); the twin measured here is training/runs/m6-twin-r/export/zap-v2.zapw, another file.

explorer.method: Re-measure, no new search: the explorer chosen by the search of attempt 2 (training/runs/m6-adaptive/eval/explorer-search-2.json, made against the safety net {"bmax":0.5,"nHalf":1}) played again against this file (safety net {"bmax":0.2,"nHalf":1}) on fresh deals. Explorer: style a, then style b, on v1, switching at a hand or once its seat has shown a number of betting events (partner in 2 against 2: the same schedule or v1 Zap). Search on selection deals (seed e5, pairs from 1360 per segment, after the earlier searches) over 1008 of 1008 candidates by successive halving against the adaptive network and the ablated network, ranked by the adaptation part. The chosen explorer then played 2000 fresh duplicate pairs per segment (seed f7, pairs 6000 to 7999, never played by an earlier attempt) against the adaptive network, the twin and the ablated network, with the Zap knobs. Gain: score of the explorer against the adaptive network minus its score against the twin, pair by pair; adaptation part: score against the adaptive network minus score against the ablated network. Pass under the rule of attempt 1 (superseded on 2026-11-22 by explorer.criterion; pass and passTwinRule): every explorer measured has a one-sided 95% upper bound of the gain over the twin of at most 1 point. passAdaptationPart: the same bound on the adaptation part, the rule of explorer.criterion.

trained.method: A network trained with PPO as a best response against the adaptive network as served when it trained (training/runs/m6-adaptive/export/zap-v2.zapw as it was then, kept since as training/runs/m6-adaptive/export/zap-v2-b0.5-h1.zapw: statistics live, safety net {"bmax":0.5,"nHalf":1}, Zap knobs), holding the other team; the explorer holds both seats of its team in 2 against 2. Start: the twin (training/explorer_init.py moves its weights on the statistics into the bias, so it starts by playing as the twin, exactly except for a small interaction term in mineiro 2 against 2: training.startFold and training.startCheck). Features v2-self: its own public statistics, the next seat's and its partner's, so it sees what the adaptive network reads about it and how many hands have gone by. One episode per match, so early play is credited with later hands. 98 PPO iterations after 5 of critic warm-up, 12367051 decisions, 3 workers and 3 learner threads, 90.1 minutes. Periodic check every 10 iterations: 200 pairs per segment (seed 3e) against the adaptive network and the ablated one. Measured on fresh deals (seed f8, pairs 0 to 1999 per segment, a seed no other bench uses), duplicate format, the explorer with neutral knobs against the adaptive network (training/runs/m6-adaptive/export/zap-v2.zapw, safety net {"bmax":0.2,"nHalf":1}), the ablated network (same file, statistics at no evidence), the twin and the second twin, all with the Zap knobs. Adaptation part: score against the adaptive network minus score against the ablated one, pair by pair (primary criterion: one-sided 95% upper bound at most 1 point). Gain over the twin: score against the adaptive network minus score against the twin; seed floor seen by this explorer: score against the second twin minus score against the twin. Style: 500 matches per segment (seed f9) of the explorer and of its start against the adaptive network, public statistics of the explorer's seats by hand of the match.

style.words: It did not learn to fake a pattern and switch. Against the adaptive network it refuses truco far more often than its start, the twin, from the first hand on: it runs on 60.9% of the raises it faces in hands 1 to 3 and on 62.5% from hand 7 on (the start: 47.7% and 54.6%), and accepts 31.2% and 25.5% of them (the start: 42.1% and 34.8%). It asks for truco about as often as the start (35.8% of its hands early, 32.5% late; the start 36.8% and 33.2%), with cards of about the same strength, and plays face down about as often. The one change over the match that the start does not show: it raises back more often late (7.8% of the raises it faces in hands 1 to 3, 11.9% from hand 7 on; the start 10.3% and 10.6%). Its matches have more hands (11% more seat hands in all, 29% more from hand 7 on). The adaptive network answers its raises almost as it answers the start's. What it found is a fixed counter to the adaptive network's betting that works just as well with the statistics at no evidence: its gain over the twin comes from the base part, and the reading part is negative.

criterion.method: Primary criterion of the explorer test: for every explorer measured on fresh deals against the file that would be served, the one-sided 95% upper bound of the adaptation part (score against the adaptive network minus score against the ablated network, the same file with the statistics at no evidence, pair by pair) is at most 1 point. The gain over the twin is reported next to it with the seed floor, for context. Verdicts recomputed from the stored fresh results of every attempt, of the trained explorer and of the control explorer when it was measured. Only the results whose adaptive file (models.adaptive.sha256) is the served file (servedModel) count, in verdicts; the results measured against earlier files are listed in history with their result file, model file and safety net, and do not count. pass is false while no explorer was measured against the served file, and while an explorer that failed against an earlier file has no verdict against the served file (pendingRemeasure lists them: a new search that passes does not replace measuring a known exploiter again). What was searched: the scripted search of attempt 1 ranked its candidates by the gain over the twin (safety net Bmax 0.5, nHalf 1); attempt 2 ranked its candidates by the adaptation part (safety net Bmax 0.5, nHalf 1); attempt 3 ranked its candidates by the adaptation part (safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1); attempt 4 measured the explorer of attempt 2 again, with no new search (safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1). The trained explorer stopped after 98 PPO iterations, 90.1 minutes (max-hours 1.5), of the 300 planned; it trained against training/runs/m6-adaptive/export/zap-v2-b0.5-h1.zapw (SHA-256 45c541c5, safety net Bmax 0.5, nHalf 1). The control explorer (trained against the twin, explorer.control) is an explorer measured too, so its verdict counts.
criterion.why: This criterion was set on 2026-11-22 after attempt 1 failed the rule written before it (gain over the twin, one-sided 95% upper bound at most 1 point), and before the trained explorer was measured. It judges the file that would be served (SHA-256 fa30e9a5, safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1): only the 4 verdicts measured against that file count; the 5 measured against earlier files are listed in explorer.criterion.history with their file and net, and do not count. Against the file with safety net Bmax 0.5, nHalf 1 (SHA-256 45c541c5), the explorer of attempt 2, trapper>bluffer@3/v1, has an adaptation part of 0.83 (from 0.50 to 1.15) points, one-sided 95% upper bound 1.10: above 1 point, so that file fails the criterion. Every explorer that failed against an earlier file was measured again against this one, on fresh deals: trapper>bluffer@3/v1 0.79 (from 0.49 to 1.09) points, upper bound 1.05. Under the old rule 1 of the 3 explorers aimed at the adaptive network and measured against this file fail (upper bounds of the gain over the twin 0.82, -1.03, 3.45 points, in the order of explorer.criterion.verdicts: scripted attempts, then the trained explorer; the control explorer trained against the twin and is left out). For the scripted explorers of attempt 1 (safety net Bmax 0.5, nHalf 1), searched for the gain over the twin, that gain (0.78, 1.15 points) is about the size of the seed floor (against the styles the second twin lands 0.80 points from the twin, from 0.56 to 1.04). For the trained explorer it is not: its seed floor is -0.29 (from -1.10 to 0.52), and its 3.35 point base part is play learned against the adaptive network's weights. It trained against the adaptive file with safety net Bmax 0.5, nHalf 1 (SHA-256 45c541c5) and was measured against this one: no explorer was trained against this file. An explorer trained the same way against the twin (explorer.control: same start, seeds and options, 98 PPO iterations) scored 62.3% against the twin on new deals (seed fa); on the same deals the trained explorer scored 60.8% against the adaptive network as served and 61.5% against the ablated one. The trained explorer's score against the adaptive network as served minus the control's against the twin is -1.51 (from -2.34 to -0.68) points (against the ablated network: -0.81, from -1.63 to 0.01), so a best response of the same budget takes less from the adaptive file as served than from the twin, and the trained explorer's base part shows no weaker base: the control in turn scores -3.54 (from -4.33 to -2.75) points against the adaptive network as served relative to the twin, so each best response is specialized to the network it trained against. The ablated network is the same file with the statistics at no evidence, so the adaptation part (score against the adaptive network minus score against the ablated one, on the same deals) holds only what the reading changes. It is also the only part the safety net acts on: without evidence the net lets nothing move, so the ablated network, and with it the base part, is the same whatever the net. Measured on the same deals (explorer.netTightening, seed f7, pairs 6000 to 7999 per segment), trapper>bluffer@3/v1 has an adaptation part of 0.94 (from 0.63 to 1.26) points, upper bound 1.21, against the file with safety net Bmax 0.5, nHalf 1 and 0.79 (from 0.49 to 1.09), upper bound 1.05, against the file with safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1: from the first to the second it changed by -0.15 (from -0.29 to -0.01) points, pair by pair, and the two ablated networks scored the same on every pair, so the base part did not change.

netTightening.method: The explorer of training/runs/m6-adaptive/eval/explorer-fresh-4.json (attempt 4, trapper>bluffer@3/v1) played again on exactly its deals (seed f7, pairs 6000 to 7999 per segment, 8000 pairs pooled, duplicate format) against four players: training/runs/m6-adaptive/export/zap-v2.zapw (safety net Bmax 0.2, nHalf 1) as served and with the statistics at no evidence, and training/runs/m6-adaptive/export/zap-v2-b0.5-h1.zapw (safety net Bmax 0.5, nHalf 1) as served and with the statistics at no evidence, all with the Zap knobs.
